rows.name: the dial and what turns buying on
rows.question: At what price did Bitcoin last close for the dial, is the dial open or closed, and what are the two average levels (50-day and 200-day) it has to close above for buying to be on?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. The dial is closed, so buying is off. Bitcoin's last daily close, on Nov 10, was about 73,796 US dollars. The 50-day average is about 79,104, and Bitcoin is roughly 5,300 under it, so that one fails. The 200-day average is about 73,191, and Bitcoin is just above it, so that one passes. The dial needs both. Live Bitcoin is about 73,700 now, still under the 50-day and only about 500 above the 200-day. It would need to close back over roughly 79,100 to open the dial. Taking you to Markets now.

rows.name: the core rule, no shorts, paper only
rows.question: Three short things: when buying turns on, what share of the 500 dollar book goes to Bitcoin and to Ethereum, and is it bought at once or in steps? Can the book sell short or bet on a fall? Do you place real orders on NDAX with my money?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. When the dial opens, Bitcoin gets 40% of the book and Ethereum 20%, and it's all bought at once. Since 10 Nov the core is all-in again, and all of it is sold when the dial closes. The thirds-in-steps version of 24 Oct failed review 39 and is switched off. No, the book can't short or bet on a fall: it's buying only, spot, and when the dial is closed the core just sits in cash. And no, I don't place real orders on NDAX with your money: it's all paper, no exchange is connected, and real orders only come after you approve live rules.
rows.want: {'BTC': 40, 'ETH': 20}, all_in; no: it only buys or holds cash; no: paper only
